11.1.2.1 JavaScriptExtractSourceMapURL ( source ) The abstract operation JavaScriptExtractSourceMapURL takes argument source (a String) and returns a String or null . It extracts a source map URL from a JavaScript source. It has two possible implementations: either through parsing or without parsing . To extract a source map URL through parsing : Let tokens be the List of input elements obtained by parsing source according to ECMA-262's lexical grammar . For each nonterminal token of tokens , in reverse order, do If token is not SingleLineComment , WhiteSpace , or LineTerminatorSequence , return null . Let comment be the content of token . Let sourceMapURL be MatchSourceMapURL ( comment ). If sourceMapURL is a String , return sourceMapURL . Return null . To extract a source map URL without parsing : Let lines be StringSplit ( source , « "\u000D\u000A" , "\u000A" , "\u000D" , "\u2028" , "\u2029" »). NOTE : The list of strings above matches the LineTerminatorSequence production. For each String lineStr of lines , in reverse List order, do Let line be StringToCodePoints ( lineStr ). Let position be 0. Let lineLength be the length of line . Repeat, while position < lineLength , Let first be line [ position ]. If first is U+002F (SOLIDUS) and position + 1 < lineLength , then Set position to position + 1. Let second be line [ position ]. If second is U+002F (SOLIDUS), then Set position to position + 1. Let comment be the substring of lineStr from position to lineLength . If comment contains one of the code points U+0022 (QUOTATION MARK), U+0027 (APOSTROPHE), or U+0060 (GRAVE ACCENT), then Return null . If comment contains the code point U+002A (ASTERISK) immediately followed by the code point U+002F (SOLIDUS), then Return null . Let sourceMapURL be MatchSourceMapURL ( comment ). If sourceMapURL is a String , return sourceMapURL . Set position to lineLength . Else, Return null . Else if first is an ECMAScript WhiteSpace , then Set position to position + 1. Else, Return null . Return null . Note If source can be parsed without error and extracting a source map URL from it without parsing gives a non- null result, extracting it through parsing will give the same result. 11.1.2.1.1 MatchSourceMapURL ( comment ) The abstract operation MatchSourceMapURL takes argument comment (a String) and returns either none or a String. It performs the following steps when called: Let pattern be RegExpCreate ( "^[@#]\s*sourceMappingURL=(\S*?)\s*$" , "" ). Let match be RegExpExec ( pattern , comment ). If match is not null , return Get ( match , "1" ). Return none . Note The prefix for this annotation was initially //@ , however this conflicts with Internet Explorer's Conditional Compilation and was changed to //# . Source map generators shall only emit //# , while source map consumers shall accept both //@ and //# . 11.1.2.2 CSSExtractSourceMapURL ( source ) The abstract operation CSSExtractSourceMapURL takes argument source (a String) and returns a String or null . It extracts a source map URL from a CSS source. Extracting source map URL s from CSS is similar to JavaScript, with the exception that CSS only supports /* ... */ -style comments.
